new_findings_today.title: /api/itinerary returns HTTP 200 but a functionally empty, broken itinerary for every single request — a long-standing latent bug that predates today, unmasked (not caused) by the 2026-08-04 AI removal
new_findings_today.detail: Section F included a valid-request content check for /api/itinerary for the first time in this skill's history (every prior run only tested its malformed/empty/empty-object error paths). The result: POST with a fully valid body ({month:12, days:5, travelerType:'family', budget:'mid-range'}) returns HTTP 200, but every day in the response has destination:'', destinationName:'', nakshiqScore:0, and a generic 'Day N' title — i.e. the itinerary has no real content at all. Reproduced 3 more times with different parameters to rule out an edge case: month=10/couple, month=5/solo, and critically month=12/family WITH explicit destinationIds=['manali','shimla','jaipur'] (three real, well-known, verified-data destinations) — ALL FOUR requests produced the identical empty-day pattern. This rules out a filtering edge case (e.g. 'no destinations score well in December') and points to the base data fetch itself failing on every call. Root cause, confirmed directly: the route's Supabase select clause requests confidence_cards(network, medical, transport, safety, best_tip, warning) — but confidence_cards only has columns destination_id/safety_rating/safety_notes/reach/sleep/fuel/weather_night/emergency/network/people_who_help. Of the 6 requested fields, only 'network' exists; medical/transport/safety/best_tip/warning do not. Reproduced the exact failure via direct SQL: SELECT network, medical, transport, safety, best_tip, warning FROM confidence_cards LIMIT 1 -> ERROR 42703: column "medical" does not exist. This means the nested PostgREST select on the whole destinations query fails, destResult.error is set — but the route NEVER CHECKS destResult.error (unlike apps/web/src/app/[locale]/explore/page.tsx, which does check and retries/throws for exactly this reason). It silently does `const destinations = destResult.data ?? []`, producing an empty destContext, which buildFallbackItinerary() then renders as generic placeholder days with a 200 status. Vercel's get_runtime_errors for /api/itinerary over the last 7 days returned ZERO errors — fully consistent with this theory, since nothing in the failure path ever throws or calls console.error. Git history shows this exact broken column list was present in the ORIGINAL feature-launch commit (3b278d69, 'feat(trip-board): Phase 4 — AI itinerary modal'), not introduced by this week's or last week's refactors. Why it was invisible until today: when the Anthropic API path was live (before the credit ran out around 2026-07-22, and before it was removed entirely 2026-08-04), the broken/empty destContext was serialized into the LLM prompt as 'DESTINATIONS DATA: []' — but the model likely still generated plausible-sounding itinerary content from its own general knowledge rather than surfacing the empty array, masking the underlying data-layer failure. Once the deterministic-only fallback became the ENTIRE response path (first silently when credit ran out, then permanently on 2026-08-04), there was no generative layer left to paper over the empty array, and the bug became directly visible in the raw output — but nothing had ever tested the valid-request path with real content assertions before today to notice.
new_findings_today.evidence: 3x additional live POST /api/itinerary probes (Oct/couple, May/solo, Dec/family+explicit destinationIds) via curl, all returning the identical empty-day pattern. Direct SQL reproduction: `SELECT network, medical, transport, safety, best_tip, warning FROM confidence_cards LIMIT 1` -> `ERROR: 42703: column "medical" does not exist`. information_schema.columns confirms confidence_cards' real column set. Direct read of apps/web/src/app/api/itinerary/route.ts lines 124-156 (the select + destContextFull mapping) and lines 355-401 (buildFallbackItinerary, showing `d?.id ?? ""` / `d?.name ?? ""` producing the empty strings observed). mcp__vercel__get_runtime_errors(routes=/api/itinerary, since=7d) -> 'No runtime errors found'. git log --follow + git show 3b278d69 -- apps/web/src/app/api/itinerary/route.ts confirms the identical select clause at the feature's original launch.
new_findings_today.recommendation: Two fixes needed, both small: (1) Correct the confidence_cards select to only request real columns — network is valid as-is; medical/transport/best_tip/warning have no obvious equivalent column today (may need a product decision on whether that data should live somewhere, or simply be dropped from the prompt/rationale text); safety could plausibly map to safety_rating + safety_notes but confirm intent before renaming. (2) Add error-checking on destResult (and trapResult) before proceeding — mirror the pattern already used in apps/web/src/app/[locale]/explore/page.tsx (check .error, log it, and either retry or throw rather than silently coalescing to []) so this exact class of bug — a broken query producing a fake-successful empty response — can never again hide from both users and monitoring simultaneously. Low-priority cleanup noticed while reading this file: the `prompt` template (route.ts:271-340) and `enrichWithRationale()` (342-353) are now dead code since the only caller was the removed Anthropic fetch block — harmless but worth deleting in the same pass for clarity. Given this has apparently been broken since the original 2026-05 launch and was only just discovered, recommend treating this as the top engineering priority from today's run — it is the single user-facing computed feature the deterministic-only itinerary refactor was specifically built to preserve, and it currently produces no real content for any request.

new_findings_today.title: Postgres statement-timeout (57014) pattern has spread significantly since last week — now hitting 11 more individual destination pages and 3 more weekend-from-city routes, not just /explore
new_findings_today.detail: Site-wide Vercel error sweep (7d) returned 35 distinct error groups today, up from 27 on 2026-08-03. /explore's own uncached-query pattern (NEW-2026-08-03-002, still confirmed unfixed via direct source read — explore/page.tsx still bypasses cached-data.ts) remains the single largest contributor (36 combined occurrences across its 3 error-message variants, continuing right up to last night 2026-08-09T20:11Z). But the SAME underlying 57014 error is now also hitting getDestination() on 11 different individual destination pages not seen in last week's sweep — varanasi (12 occurrences, ongoing through 08-09), valley-of-flowers, jaipur, kalpa (via getMonthData), mandi, rishikesh, mechuka, kumarakom, shantiniketan, kedarnath, netarhat (last one as recently as 2026-08-09T23:21Z, i.e. a few hours before this run) — plus 3 NEW weekend-from-city routes (mumbai, hyderabad, bangalore, joining last week's delhi) and a brand-new error source, fetchAllRows(local_stays) failing during /api/search-index's ISR revalidation. IMPORTANT DISTINCTION FROM LAST WEEK'S FRAMING: unlike /explore, the individual destination page's getDestination() function (apps/web/src/app/[locale]/destination/[id]/page.tsx:150-203) is NOT a caching-bypass bug — it already has a 24h ISR revalidate window, 3 retry attempts with backoff, and deliberately throws (rather than silently degrading) on a persistent timeout so Next.js doesn't cache a false 404. That this well-designed, already-cached code path is ALSO now timing out under load suggests the underlying Postgres instance is under broader contention than a single bad query pattern — possibly correlated with the new agent-based cron load (refresh-stay-picks-agent, road-sweep-agent, sos-auto-reverify all added/changed 2026-08-04) or concurrent ISR regeneration bursts (the 2026-08-06 build failure, commit a48b1674, was explicitly attributed to 'three full 5,406-page prerenders running concurrently against the same Supabase instance'). None of today's 10 randomly sampled destinations hit this — all 10 returned 200 (one with an expected cold-ISR-cache first-hit delay, confirmed via cache-HIT on re-request, not a timeout). The site is NOT visibly broken; this remains an intermittent, self-recovering, low-single-digit-user-count pattern. But the trend direction — more error groups, more distinct pages affected, spreading to already-well-cached code paths — is the part worth flagging clearly rather than re-filing as 'unchanged.'

new_findings_today.recommendation: The /explore fix recommended last week still stands and is still the single biggest lever (route its destinations/states/coords query through apps/web/src/lib/cached-data.ts). business_summary.headline: Today's audit found a serious, previously-invisible problem: the trip itinerary planner — the one remaining 'build me a plan' feature after last week's move away from paid AI — has actually been silently broken since it first launched months ago. It returns what looks like a successful result, but the plan itself is empty. Last week's AI chat outage is now fully resolved (the feature was intentionally retired rather than paid for again), and the database slowdown flagged last week has grown rather than shrunk.

traffic_lights.why: Every request to build an itinerary succeeds (no error shown) but comes back with a blank plan — no destinations, no real day-by-day content. This has apparently been broken since the feature first launched; it was hidden until now because the AI layer used to paper over the gap with its own general knowledge. Now that the AI layer is gone, the underlying problem is fully exposed. Root cause is identified and the fix is small (a data query is asking for fields that don't exist) — this is not a rebuild, just a targeted repair.

Resolved — but by removing the feature entirely (founder decision on 2026-08-04 to stop paying for metered AI), not by fixing the billing issue flagged last week. There is no longer anything that can run out of credit; a new build-time check makes sure it can't quietly come back.
